dataset.name: ORNL FACE Final Harvest, 2009, with data on leaf characteristics and tree mass
description: During the final year of the Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) free-air CO2 enrichment (FACE) experiment, 16 trees were felled and processed during July 2009. The trees had been grown for 12 years in ambient or elevated CO2. Two data sets are reported. Leaf characteristics (leaf mass per unit area, leaf thickness, average leaf size, carbon and nitrogen concentrations) are reported for each 1-meter section of the tree crowns in data set "Canopy_subsamples.csv". The measurements were made on approximately 20 subsamples collected from each 1-meter section of the canopy. Wood dry mass, total tree height, basal area, total leaf mass and leaf area are reported in "Tree_harvest.csv", based on field measurements of fresh mass and dry mass to fresh mass ratio of subsamples. The ORNL FACE experiment, including photos of the harvesting activity, is described at: https://richnorby.org/home/face-home/.

spatialCoverage.description: The Oak Ridge National Laboratory FACE Experiment was located on the Oak Ridge National Environmental Research Park in eastern Tennessee on an old terrace of the Clinch River.

funder.name: U.S. DOE > Office of Science > Basic Energy Sciences (BES)

measurementTechnique:
16 trees were from the FACE experiment were felled and processed during July 2009. After felling, tree height was measured with a tape measure, and 1-m sections of the crown were marked off starting from the top of the tree. Circumference of the bole at 1.3 m and 4.0 m height was measured and the measurement converted to cross-sectional area. From each 1-meter section approximately 20 leaves were randomly collected as a subsample. Dry mass, area, and thickness of the subsampled leaves were measured, and the leaves
were analyzed for nitrogen and carbon content. Remaining leaves were removed from each section, oven-dried, and weighed. Leaf area of the section was determined from leaf mass and leaf mass per unit area of subsampled leaves. Total tree leaf mass and leaf area is the sum of the 1-meter sections. Wood dry mass was measured from field measurements of fresh weight of bole sections and branches and the fresh mass to dry mass of slices from each section, which were weighed fresh in the field and after oven drying.
The ORNL FACE experiment, including photos of the harvesting activity is described at: https://richnorby.org/home/face-home/
